sources.note: Hendrycks & Gimpel 2016 — GELU = x·Φ(x); the sampled values and derivatives in the figure are the chapter's printed numbers from this construction.
Dauphin et al. 2017 — gated linear units, the W_g/W_v split the figure traces.
Shazeer 2020 — SwiGLU and the 3·d_model·m = 8d_model² budget that sets m = 8d_model/3.

figures.title: Two projections, one gate, one product
figures.caption: A gated linear unit splits the up-projection into a gate matrix W_g and a value matrix W_v, applies Swish to the gate, and multiplies the two elementwise before the down-projection. Holding the parameter budget at 8d_model² requires m = 8d_model/3, about 2.67d_model, so the scratch space is two-thirds as wide as the plain four-times FFN.
figures.alt: A lane starts at x with width d_model. W_g and W_v each project d_model to m = 8d_model/3. Swish is applied to the gate, the gate and value are multiplied elementwise, W_d projects m back to d_model, and the result is added to x. The residual bypass runs above the stages. Labels give m = 10,922.67 at d_model = 4,096 and 3·d_model·m = 8d_model² parameters.

data.note: Holding 8d_model²: 3·d_model·m = 8d_model² gives m = 8d_model/3 = 10,922.67 at d_model = 4,096; LLaMA rounds to 11,008, a multiple of 256; the exact width is about 2.67d_model. Linear multiply-adds stay at 8d_model², the gate adds a sigmoid and an elementwise multiply per element, and the scratch width falls from 4d_model to 8d_model/3.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to trace the gated projection.

steps.label: Project the gate and value halves: W_g x and W_v x, each width m.
Bend the gate with Swish; leave the value linear.
Contract with W_d and add to the residual stream.

figures.title: ReLU and GELU at the chapter's sample points
figures.caption: Sampled at the points the chapter prints. ReLU's column is exactly zero with zero derivative for every negative input; GELU dips to -0.1587 at x = -1 and keeps a nonzero derivative there, while its derivative at x = 0 is 0.5.
figures.alt: A five-row table with columns x, ReLU, GELU, and GELU derivative. At x = -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, ReLU gives 0, 0, 0, 0, 1. GELU gives -0.0040, -0.0455, -0.1587, 0, 0.8413. The derivative gives -0.0119, -0.0852, -0.0833, 0.5, 1.0833. The negative dip and the nonzero negative-side derivative are the difference from ReLU.

data.note: GELU(x) = xΦ(x), and Φ(x) is the probability that a standard normal draw falls below x; the output is the input scaled by that probability. Its derivative is Φ(x)+xφ(x). The derivative is zero at the minimum near x = -0.75 and approaches zero as x falls. GELU lacks ReLU's exact zero-gradient region but still saturates; a unit consistently below -3 learns slowly.
